summary: Verified fix for 'Cannot access isInFy before initialization' on Dashboard. Logged in as admin/admin123, Dashboard rendered cleanly with 0 page errors and 0 console errors. FY selector (data-testid=dashboard-fy-selector) is present in header, defaults to FY 2026-27 (the FY containing today per system date). Changing FY to 2025 → header/subtitles update to 'FY 2025-26' and charts re-render; changing to 2024 → 'FY 2024-25' shown; no throws. Monthly Sales and Monthly Production charts show month labels in FY order Apr 26, May 26, ... Mar 27. Sales Forecast modal opens via clicking a month row in the Next-6-Months table; product-mix donut slices ([data-testid=mix-slice-*]) render; single click on a slice filters the SO table to that product only (Filtered by <product> banner visible + Clear filter link), and Ctrl-click on a second slice adds it to the selection without errors. No 'isInFy', 'Cannot access', or 'ReferenceError' anywhere.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Fix for TDZ error on Dashboard (isInFy used before declaration) is confirmed resolved. FY block correctly declared before pendingJobCards/shortages/customerAggMap. FY selector is a styled native <select> — automate via evaluate to dispatch 'change' event, not select_option on the wrapper div. rca of the issue: TDZ (temporal dead zone) issue where isInFy was referenced in pendingJobCards/shortages/customerAggMap computations that ran earlier in the component body than the const isInFy declaration. Fix: moved fyStartYear state + monthBuckets + fyMonthKeys + isInFy block to the top of the Dashboard component before any consumer. Verified only a single 'const isInFy' declaration exists in Dashboard.tsx.
